clue.text: It could be construed as what makes us single

definitions.text: It could be construed as what makes us single

indicators.note: construed here means read in another way, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rueful thought about why some of us never find a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be construed' rearranges US SINGLE, and the whole clue doubles as the definition: plainness might be what keeps us unattached.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainness of looks is jokingly offered as the reason someone stays unattached, so the whole clue describes the quality.

clue.text: What's right in a youngster is nevertheless wrong

indicators.note: in places the letter for right inside the word for a youngster

parts.note: a tot is a small child
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A paradox: something correct inside a child is still mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: TORT is the legal term for a civil wrong, such as negligence or trespass.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a tort is a civil wrong for which damages can be claimed.

clue.text: Market town for pastel reproduction

indicators.note: a reproduction is a copy made anew, so the word's letters are made again in a new order

explanation.surface: A painter heads to a country town to copy a pastel drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproduction' rearranges PASTEL. Historically a staple was a town granted the right to hold a market in a chief commodity such as wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a staple was a town with royal rights of trade, a market centre for a principal commodity.

clue.text: Disconnected belligerent

definitions.meaning: made of scraps and bits, not joined up or coherent
keen to fight, spoiling for a scrap

explanation.surface: A soldier cut off from command and spoiling for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fragmentary, made of scraps, and spoiling for a fight, from scrap as a brawl.

clue.text: Beauty treatment for alien inhabitant of the universe

indicators.note: an inhabitant lives within, so the alien goes inside the adjective

parts.note: cosmic means relating to the universe
ET is the film's extra-terrestrial, a standard crossword alien

explanation.surface: A space visitor seeks a makeover at the salon.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a space visitor at the salon; 'inhabitant' is the containment signal, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic as a noun is a beauty product or treatment applied to improve appearance.

clue.text: Fan creates a stir about a timeless story

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: less time means the letter T for time is removed from the word

parts.note: fiction is an invented story
ado is fuss or a stir

explanation.surface: An enthusiast causes a commotion over an ageless tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' is both signal and its own instruction: less time, so the letter for time goes; 'about' links the stir to the story.
explanation.definitionFit: An aficionado is a devoted enthusiast, a keen fan of some pursuit.

clue.text: Shipwrecked mariner was off course

indicators.note: off means astray, so the letters of the word wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor wrecked because he strayed from his route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was off' rearranges COURSE. Robinson Crusoe is Defoe's castaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinson Crusoe is the castaway hero of Defoe's novel, wrecked on a desert island.

clue.text: Without certain knowledge, it's costing a bomb

indicators.note: a bomb blows things apart, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone unsure of the price grumbles that it costs a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bomb' rearranges COSTING A; the surface reads 'costing a bomb' as very expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic holds that knowledge of God, or certainty on a question, cannot be had.

clue.text: University evokes old times for many

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
taken as written
D is the Roman numeral 500, a large number

explanation.surface: An ancient university calls up memories of bygone days for lots of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'times' looks temporal beside 'old', but it is the multiplication sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford is the ancient English university city and its university.

clue.text: Reportedly failed to see in the fog

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: missed means failed to see or notice

explanation.surface: Someone says they missed something because of poor visibility.
explanation.walkthrough: MISSED and MIST sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Mist is a thin fog, low cloud of fine droplets reducing visibility.

clue.text: Chemist called to give agricultural help

indicators.note: called means spoken, so the phrase is what is heard

parts.note: a farm assist, help on the farm

explanation.surface: A druggist is summoned to lend a hand on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, FARM ASSIST gives the dispenser of medicines.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispensing chemist in Britain is a pharmacist, who prepares and sells medicines.

clue.text: Soldier's signal to go on an errand of mercy

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are British Army soldiers, plus the 's
a cue is a signal to act

explanation.surface: A soldier hears the signal to set off on a mission to save lives.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps; with the 's it gives RES.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescue is a saving mission, a journey made to help those in danger.

clue.text: Cautious about girl getting a drink

indicators.note: about means around, so the cautious word wraps the girl

parts.note: chary means wary or cautious
Donna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A wary man hesitates as a woman orders a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cautious about girl' reads like a character sketch, but 'about' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chardonnay is a white wine made from the grape of that name.

clue.text: Gone off course before finding cause of illness

parts.note: a path is a course or route

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A traveller strays from the route before picking up a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone off course' reads as straying, but 'off' signals rearranging the first word, and 'before' puts the route first.
explanation.definitionFit: A pathogen is a bacterium, virus or other microbe that causes disease.

clue.text: Goddess fails to finish a first course

indicators.note: failing to finish means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a starter is the first course of a meal

explanation.surface: A diner leaves the opening dish of a meal uneaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails to finish' drops the last R from STARTER. Astarte was the Phoenician goddess of fertility and love.
explanation.definitionFit: Astarte is a Phoenician and Semitic goddess of love and fertility.

clue.text: Former PM and band leader

definitions.meaning: Edward Heath was British Conservative Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974
a namesake led a famous British big band from the 1940s

explanation.surface: A one-time prime minister who also ran a dance band.
explanation.walkthrough: The PM (1970-74) and the big-band leader were different men with the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the 1970s Conservative premier and to a famous British big-band leader.

clue.text: Officer's label on a figure

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding, the possessive adding no letter
a tag is a label
taken as written

explanation.surface: An officer's name tag is pinned to a diagram.
explanation.walkthrough: OC, Officer Commanding, is a British military abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An octagon is a plane figure with eight sides and angles.

clue.text: Dutiful child of Ruth (that's part of scripture)

parts.note: in the Bible Obed is the son of Ruth and Boaz
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A biblical aside about a well-behaved son of Ruth.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads as an aside, but it supplies IE and NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Obedient means doing as one is told, so dutiful in obeying.

clue.text: Priests are in chaos, but carry on regardless

indicators.note: chaos means disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The clergy are in disarray but keep going anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are in chaos' rearranges PRIESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to keep going stubbornly despite difficulty or opposition.

clue.text: Hedge featured in abstract painting style

parts.note: read as H, the pencil grade for hard, followed by EDGE, so the answer written in brief gives the clue word

explanation.surface: A garden hedge appears in a modern abstract canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: Abbreviate the first word of the answer to H, as on a hard pencil, and you get the clue's garden boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-edge painting is a 1950s-60s abstract style using crisp, clean-edged areas of flat colour.

clue.text: See a limb half 25

parts.note: an arm is a limb

indicators.note: half means only the first three letters of the answer to 25 are used

explanation.surface: Observe one limb, half horrified.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Armagh in Northern Ireland is the seat of the Primate of All Ireland. 25 is AGHAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's diocese, and Armagh is the archiepiscopal seat of Ireland's primate.

clue.text: Soft sweet stuff, but it's not genuine

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
honey is sweet stuff made by bees

explanation.surface: A gooey confection that turns out to be fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoney means fake, sham or insincere.

clue.text: Bill for when Charles becomes King?

definitions.meaning: a bill is a printed notice or placard put up in public
read as ..., after Elizabeth Regina, whose reign Charles's accession would follow

explanation.surface: A notice printed for the coronation of a new king.
explanation.walkthrough: Written in Elizabeth II's reign: ER is her royal cipher, so the reign of King Charles would come after (post) ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A poster is a bill, a printed notice displayed on a wall or board.

clue.text: Chap employed in producing an issue?

definitions.text: Chap employed in producing an issue?

indicators.note: employed in means set to work inside, so the chap goes inside the other letters
producing means making something new, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a man is a chap

explanation.surface: A man hired to help bring out a publication.
explanation.walkthrough: An issue here is a publication; the whole clue describes a scribe or secretary who writes out documents, while 'producing' and 'employed in' work the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis is a secretary or scribe hired to write out or copy text for another.

clue.text: One may be out on it or out when it's off

definitions.text: One may be out on it or out when it's off

parts.words: One may be out on it or out when it's off
parts.note: an accused person may be freed on it awaiting trial, and in cricket a batsman is out when the little crosspiece is knocked off the stumps

explanation.surface: A riddle about being free yet dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bails sit on top of the stumps; dislodging one gets the batsman out.
explanation.definitionFit: Bail is both security for a defendant's release and a crosspiece atop the cricket stumps.

clue.text: Bundle of mischief

definitions.meaning: a large tied package of hay or goods
an old sense meaning evil or harm, as in baleful

explanation.surface: A small heap of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a tied bundle of hay or goods, and archaically evil or woe.

clue.text: How mule looks when bag has to be searched?

indicators.note: searching the words finds the letters lying within them

explanation.surface: A drug courier's face when customs open the luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: A mule here is a drug smuggler, who would look horrified at a bag search.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means horrified or shocked, the look of someone caught out.

clue.text: Trading about a quarter, but it's on the increase

indicators.note: about means around, so the trading word wraps the compass point

parts.note: selling is trading goods
W, west, is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: Business revolves around a quarter, and it is growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts W inside SELLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Swelling means growing larger, expanding or rising.
